title: tool-calling: execution ergonomics for parallel multi-tool calls, result injection, and retries
author: Aisha Patel
description:
Motivation: Improve ergonomics and reliability for multi-tool flows invoked in parallel from the OpenAI-compat API and native SDKs. Users have reported surprising semantics when multiple tools are called in parallel and their results are injected into the prompt: inconsistent ordering, partial retries leading to duplicate injections, and difficulty specifying per-tool retry policies. This PR standardizes execution semantics, simplifies the developer-facing APIs, and adds safety for result injection and retry behavior.

Design summary: 1) Introduce an execution orchestrator that tracks tool-call groups and assigns deterministic ordering metadata so injected results are stable across retries. 2) Add a per-tool retry policy with two modes (idempotent, best-effort) surfaced in the OpenAI-compat layer and SDKs. 3) Make parallel tool calls composable: callers can mark tool-calls as a single composite operation (useful for batched tools) so that retries operate at the composite level rather than individual tool RPCs. 4) Streaming stability: ensure tool-result chunks are emitted in stable order during streaming responses and add checkpoints to allow resume/replay without duplication. 5) Backwards compatibility: default behaviors match previous semantics for single-tool calls; multi-tool parallel flows are opt-in via the new annotate() wrapper or the openai-compatible "tool_group" field.

Implementation notes: - core/serving/tool_execution.py: new Orchestrator class (stateless controller + idempotency token helpers) and deterministic ordering assignment using request-scoped sequence ids. - api/openai_compat/handlers.py: accepts optional "tool_group" metadata and new per-tool "retry_mode" param; converts previous ad-hoc behavior into orchestrated calls. - sdk/python/redwood/tools.py and sdk/typescript: expose Tools.annotate_group() helper and default retry policies. - tests/tool_calling/test_parallel_injection.py: coverage for ordering, injection dedupe, and retry semantics. - observability: added metrics tool_call.group_latency, tool_call.retry_count, tool_call.duplicate_injection_detected and tracing spans for orchestration decisions. - docs/tool-calling.md: updated examples for parallel groups, streaming checkpoints, and migration guide.

Compatibility and migration: Existing integrations that call a single tool are unaffected. Integrations that relied on nondeterministic ordering for parallel tool calls should opt-in to stable ordering via tool_group or annotate(). We included a migration guide and compatibility shim that preserves legacy behavior when tool_group is absent.

Testing and rollout: Unit and integration tests added. CI showed a flaky e2e test initially; the pipeline was rerun and passed. We rolled this out behind a feature flag (tool_calling_stable_parallel) for 2 weeks before flipping for all customers. We also added a canary that exercises long-tail streaming tool outputs.

Impact: Reduced duplicated tool-injection incidents in our staging environment and improved latency for common 2-tool parallel flows due to reduced retry amplification and more efficient batching of composite tool calls.

review_comments: Daniel Kim: Request changes - can you ensure ordering metadata is stable across proxies? Observability should include origin endpoint to help debug ordering issues.
Aisha Patel (author): Reply - added request-scoped sequence ids and included origin tags in tracing spans; updated observability section in the PR.
Marta Lopez: Question - how does retry_mode interact with composite tool groups? Should the default be idempotent for known-idempotent tools?

Aisha Patel (author): Reply - retry_mode defaults to best-effort to avoid surprising long tail delays; added SDK helper to set default per-organization. Added docs explaining how to mark tools as idempotent.
Ethan Zhao: Approval - tests look solid and the migration path is clear. Recommend we monitor tool_call.duplicate_injection_detected metric closely after rollout.
ci_checks: benchmarks: perf-regression check passed (2-tool p50 -12% latency)
release_notes:
Improvements: Stable execution semantics for parallel multi-tool calls; deterministic ordering for tool result injection; new per-tool retry_mode (idempotent|best-effort); SDK helpers annotate_group() and tool_group support in OpenAI-compat layer; streaming checkpoints to avoid duplicate injections.
Migration: Single-tool calls unchanged. Multi-tool parallel flows should opt-in via annotate_group()/tool_group. See docs/tool-calling.md for migration steps.
